items.titleEn: Gold, silver plunge as hotter U.S. inflation raises prospect of larger Fed rate hike - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Tuesday, as stronger-than-expected U.S. consumer inflation reinforced expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December and raised the possibility of a larger policy adjustment. Treasury yields and the dollar advanced following the inflation report, placing renewed pressure on precious metals despite another decline in crude oil prices and reduced concerns about immediate military escalation involving Iran. Spot gold was trading near $4,031.80 an ounce, down $107.60, or 2.60%, while spot silver was trading near $51.410, down $1.894, or 3.55%. The U.S. Labor Department reported Tuesday that the consumer price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.4% in October, exceeding economists' expectations for a 0.3% gain. The increase was slower than September's 0.6% rise but showed that inflationary pressure remained persistent. Core consumer prices, excluding food and energy, increased 0.3%, above expectations for a 0.2% gain and matching the monthly increases recorded in August and September. The stronger underlying reading reinforced concerns that the Federal Reserve may need to maintain restrictive monetary policy for longer than previously anticipated. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not publish most October annual inflation rates because the October 2025 federal government shutdown prevented the collection of comparable data. As a result, the latest report provides no directly comparable annual headline or core inflation reading for October. That limitation increases the importance of the monthly figures and the underlying price components in evaluating the near-term inflation outlook.

items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Investigations into whether Nvidia's CEO was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort" are raising questions about the future of the chipmaker, which became one of the world's most valuable companies by providing technology that powered the artificial intelligence boom. Jensen Huang has been synonymous with Nvidia since he co-founded it more than 30 years ago. The company now faces potential damage to its reputation and stock price, uncertainty over a possible successor and new scrutiny from shareholders and elected officials.
